title: Avoiding Double Trapping in Drainage Systems
description: Installing two P-traps in series on a single fixture drain line—a scenario known as double trapping—is a pitfall that severely impairs drainage performance. Some installers incorrectly assume adding a second trap offers double protection against sewer gas, but it actually creates an unvented air pocket trapped between two water seals. This air lock restricts water movement, traps debris, and leads to chronic slow draining or complete blockages. Professional plumbers ensure every fixture relies on a single, properly vented P-trap to maintain smooth flow while reliably sealing out sewer gas.

Avoiding Double Trapping in Drainage Systems

Installing two P-traps in series on a single fixture drain line—a scenario known as double trapping—is a pitfall that severely impairs drainage performance. Some installers incorrectly assume adding a second trap offers double protection against sewer gas, but it actually creates an unvented air pocket trapped between two water seals. This air lock restricts water movement, traps debris, and leads to chronic slow draining or complete blockages. Professional plumbers ensure every fixture relies on a single, properly vented P-trap to maintain smooth flow while reliably sealing out sewer gas.
